task: Use the ROME CounterFact corpus in an adapted in-context first-token task. Include 24 hashed unique subjects with one-token alphabetic true and new objects, at most two subjects per relation. Use the canonical prompt, the first paraphrase and the first neighborhood prompt from every selected case. Select without model outcomes. An old or revised fact precedes each query. The altered fact is a counterfactual instruction.
hypothesis: A transition with a large effect after per-head RMS normalization selects a better adjacent pair of layer-28 recurrent heads than response energy before normalization, matrix norm or fixed heads 28 and 29. For the selected pair, approximate its action on the four transported recipient queries using rank-one response SVD. Use only raw internal states, no output labels or logits in the selection.
controls: Raw response selection and fixed position use exactly the same response SVD. Matrix-norm selection uses a standard rank-one state SVD. Each sends 512 FP32 factors plus a head-pair index if selected dynamically. Also test old/full donor, all donor recurrent matrices, complete donor matrix at one layer, and both complete matrices of the selected pair. Every sparse arm leaves recipient convolution and attention unchanged.
gate: The normalized primary must gain at least four of 48 changed free-token answers over the best equally sparse or old control, retain every previously correct neighbor and recover at least half of the positive full-donor improvement. Report the pairwise token preference separately. Cases and metrics precede inference. All input data remain with the original authors.
scope: Local M5 four-bit 9B, 1200-second pilot, one engineering repair allowance. Donor prefill and recipient suffix trace are available in this causal diagnostic. No deployment or time-saving claim.
